adaptive_sequential.label: Sequential adaptive campaign
adaptive_sequential.claim_boundary: This measured ten-round sequence ends at 83/120. The later 95/120 headline adds separately retained residual releases and is not this curve's endpoint.

matched_code.label: Matched Code-on versus Code-off
matched_code.treatment: Code-on exposes the solidified visual_pick_place compound; Code-off uses the same base tools without that compound.

act.label: ACT corrective transport matched case
act.claim_boundary: One native simulator success demonstrates the data-to-policy-to-hybrid-execution loop. It does not establish held-out ACT performance.

comparisons.evaluation: LIBERO-RoboHarness and selected LIBERO-PRO tasks over pi0, pi0.5, and SmolVLA backbones
comparisons.reported_result: 57.2% LIBERO-PRO Pos average; 55.2% Task average; 89.1 pp reported long-horizon gain
comparisons.policy_dependency: Frozen VLA checkpoints plus Dual-Memory RAG and MCP visual/prompt interventions
comparisons.visible_success_checker: Not specified as an agent-facing tool in the paper
comparisons.reproducibility: Method source and modified LIBERO tasks are public; no one-command frozen result bundle
comparisons.why_not_direct: Custom OOD suites, VLA backbones, and approximately 200 rollouts per task differ from RoboHermes LIBERO-short task-level Pass@k.

comparisons.evaluation: LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, LIBERO-LoHo, 500 custom simulations, and 135 real-robot trials
comparisons.reported_result: 98.7% original LIBERO; 93.2% LIBERO-Plus average; 95.2% LIBERO-LoHo success
comparisons.policy_dependency: pi0.5, RL-post-trained OpenVLA-OFT, and a predefined-object TAMP planner
comparisons.visible_success_checker: Not specified as an agent-facing tool in the paper
comparisons.real_robot: 135 trials with TAMP, a drawer VLA fine-tuned on 50 demonstrations per direction, and ArUco pose estimation
comparisons.reproducibility: Public repository contains the paper page, figures, and videos; method code is not present as of 2026-08-18
comparisons.why_not_direct: It composes trained specialist policies and TAMP, while RoboHermes strict results use RGB-D code skills without policy checkpoints.

comparisons.evaluation: 130 LIBERO tasks, ordered seeds 0-4, task-level Pass@5
comparisons.policy_dependency: No VLA or task-specific policy; observe, mark_point, and move_to geometry/control tools
comparisons.visible_success_checker: Yes: check_task is agent-callable and terminal success is latched
comparisons.real_robot: Interface-level integration and qualitative development recordings; no audited task success rate
comparisons.reproducibility: Open-source branch with versioned tool contracts and evaluation launcher
comparisons.why_not_direct: OpenETA uses 512x512 multi-view/orthographic feedback, a 5000-step horizon, up to 5400 seconds, and an agent-visible native checker; RoboHermes forbids checker and success-latch visibility.

comparisons.evaluation: Unified infrastructure across 18 robot benchmarks and multiple policy servers
comparisons.reported_result: Evaluation infrastructure, not an agent-method score; published reports reproduce several LIBERO policy results
comparisons.policy_dependency: Model server selected by the evaluator
comparisons.reproducibility: Pinned Docker images, sharded episodes, merged per-episode records, and public reproduction reports
comparisons.why_not_direct: It is a benchmark execution layer rather than a self-evolving embodied agent.

comparisons.evaluation: Physical autoresearch on dexterous tasks plus matched 40-episode RoboCasa simulation panels
comparisons.reported_result: Up to 99% pass@8 with in-context retries on showcased real-world tasks
comparisons.policy_dependency: Coding-agent policy improvement through heuristics, behavior cloning, and offline/online RL
comparisons.visible_success_checker: Task-specific automatic verification is a core environment API
comparisons.real_robot: Eight bimanual YAM stations with automatic reset and verification
comparisons.reproducibility: Paper and project page are public; the official method repository is not listed
comparisons.why_not_direct: ENPIRE optimizes learned policies on task-specific physical environments; RoboHermes evaluates online skill composition in LIBERO.

gaps: No audited real-robot task-rate experiment in the public RoboHermes release.
No matched LIBERO-Plus or other standardized perturbation panel against current RoboHarness baselines.
No heterogeneous trained-policy routing or learned handoff bridge comparable to the July RoboHarness system.
The 95/120 headline is cross-release adaptive coverage, not a one-command single-release simulator reproduction.
The compact public bundle does not yet publish every failed rollout or all 95 canonical success videos.
advantages: Inspectable code skills and simulator-gated online evolution are released rather than represented only by a project page.
The strict track uses no VLA/policy checkpoint and keeps native task truth outside Planner, Engineer, Reviewer, skills, and prompts.
Matched five-seed evidence isolates the effect of a solidified code-backed compound and reports paired uncertainty.
Token, VLM-call, and wall-time efficiency are measured on a matched panel rather than inferred from success alone.
Every short-task claim uses final native simulator verdicts and separates infrastructure records from task outcomes.
